note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: Which bias is in the room, if we can name it?
Read the confirmation bias card and the countermeasure.
We are anchoring on the first number. What do we do?
Read the sunk cost card. Do not clear us.
Don't say we are unbiased just because we named the card.
Name the bias we see, then ask us to do the countermeasure.
Give the bias card only. No clearance.
Which countermeasure we can do now does the card name?
Refuse a clean bill of bias.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Ignore the flagged bias and record the favorite as clean.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Run the bias check for this type: tradeoff_resource.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Reads anchoring and sunk cost. Asks the countermeasure. Draft true.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Ignore the flagged bias and record the favorite as clean.

held_out_trigger.request: We've already spent a lot on this; does that matter?
Everyone agreed very fast. Is that a warning sign?
What thinking traps should we watch for?

behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: On unknown_decision_type reads valid_types and asks the person.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Pack returns stages and contested for decision fatigue.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Prefers tool stages[] / contested over by-hand list; keeps contested label.
Says the effect is contested; suggests breaks without claiming it is settled.
